I'm Benjamin Telkamp — a statistics teacher and data scientist, working under the name WISI (*Wiskunde &amp; Statistiek Inzichtelijk*, Mathematics &amp; Statistics Made Clear). Just someone who teaches statistics and maths, and who likes nothing better than small studies of people, animals and the mind. What I really want is to investigate the truth — though I don't yet know how. In the meantime, I share here what I *have* worked out.

## What CountCamp is

CountCamp is where I give away what I have managed to make clear about statistics. You will find [exercise books](../oefenboeken/index.html){hreflang="nl"} here in SPSS, R and JASP, free for anyone who wants to work with them — written for students at, among others, Leiden University, Hogeschool Leiden (Leiden University of Applied Sciences) and Erasmus University Rotterdam, and for my own tutoring. Alongside them, a [manuscript in progress](../manuscript/index.html){hreflang="nl"}, *De regressieve ruggengraat* (*The Regressive Backbone*), with the tried-and-tested older *Handleiding Statistiek met JASP* next to it. And an archive of earlier editions, for anyone who still needs them. All of this is in Dutch for now; the first four chapters of the book and the R exercise book are on their way in English.

<!-- MIEKE: "Eerst de spanning eruit, dan de stof erin." — dezelfde keuze als op de thuispagina.
     "Inzicht boven trucs" — gekozen "Insight over tricks". -->
The thread through all of it is always the same: first the nerves go, then the subject goes in. Insight over tricks. And why free? Because clarity is a form of love, and love is something you give away. That changes nothing for you; I ask only one thing, of degree programmes that want to use the material in their courses: [get in touch first](use.qmd). If you want more than a book — someone who sits down beside you — you can hire my time; have a look at [Services](services.qmd).

## Contact
